## Tests and services

- [BISmark](https://measurementlab.net/tests/bismark/): Allowed people to host a home router that also tests network performance over time.
- [Glasnost](https://measurementlab.net/tests/glasnost/): Glasnost tested for application-specific blocking or throttling, and was decommissioned on 07/07/2017. The source code is still available.
- [Neubot](https://measurementlab.net/tests/neubot/): DASH is designed to measure the quality of tested networks by emulating a video streaming player.
- [NPAD (Network Path & Application Diagnostics)](https://measurementlab.net/tests/npad/): Diagnosed common problems that impact last-mile broadband networks.
- [OONI Probe](https://measurementlab.net/tests/ooni/): Measured specific use cases of network interference.
- [MobiPerf](https://measurementlab.net/tests/mobiperf/): Measured network performance on mobile platforms.
- [Pathload2](https://measurementlab.net/tests/pathload2/): Tested the available bandwidth of an Internet connection until it was decommissioned from the M-Lab platform on 12/21/2012. However, the data and source code are still available.
- [SamKnows](https://measurementlab.net/tests/samknows/): M-Lab hosted the off-net servers for SamKnows performance testing used in the FCC's Measuring Broadband America Program from 2009-2019.
- [Shaperprobe](https://measurementlab.net/tests/shaperprobe/): Shaperprobe attempted to measure traffic shaping. Shaperpobe was decommissioned from the M-Lab fleet on 5/11/2015.
- [Windrider](https://measurementlab.net/tests/windrider/): Attempted to detect whether a mobile provider was performing application or service specific differentiation until it was decommissioned on 01/17/2013. The source code is still available.
- [Wehe](https://measurementlab.net/tests/wehe/): Wehe uses your device to exchange Internet traffic recorded from real, popular apps like YouTube and Spotify, and attempts to tell you whether your ISP is giving different performance to an app's…
- [Reverse Traceroute](https://measurementlab.net/tests/reverse_traceroute/): Measures the network path back to a user from selected network endpoints.
- [MSAK](https://measurementlab.net/tests/msak/): MSAK (Measurement Swiss-Army Knife) implements a configurable Websocket-based throughput measurement protocol, and a UDP-based latency measurement protocol.
- [Packet Header Service (PCAP)](https://measurementlab.net/tests/pcap/): Collects packet headers for all incoming TCP flows and saves each stream of packet captures into a per-stream .pcap file.
- [TCP INFO](https://measurementlab.net/tests/tcp-info/): Collects statistics about the TCP connections running on the M-Lab platform using tcp-info.
- [HERMES](https://measurementlab.net/tests/hermes/): Detects performance degradations affecting groups of Internet users, and the network segments associated with them.
- [NDT (Network Diagnostic Tool)](https://measurementlab.net/tests/ndt/): Tests your connection speed, and provides a sophisticated diagnosis of problems limiting speed.
- [Paris Traceroute](https://measurementlab.net/tests/paris_traceroute/): Collected network path information for every connection to the M-Lab 1.0 platform.
- [scamper1 Schema](https://measurementlab.net/tests/traceroute/scamper1/)
- [SideStream](https://measurementlab.net/tests/sidestream/): Collected web100 statistics about the TCP connections running on the M-Lab 1.0 platform.
- [Traceroute](https://measurementlab.net/tests/traceroute/): Collects network path information for every connection to the M-Lab platform.

## Knowledge Base

### Getting Started

- [Welcome to M-Lab: Open Internet Measurement](https://measurementlab.net/kb/welcome-to-mlab): An introduction to what M-Lab is, what it measures, and how its open data can help you understand internet performance.

### Understanding Measurement

- [Understanding Speed Test Results](https://measurementlab.net/kb/understanding-speed-test-results): Why different speed tests produce different results, and what those differences reveal about your internet connection.
- [FAQ: Test Rate Limits](https://measurementlab.net/kb/test-rate-limits): As a first approximation, M-Lab allows 40 tests per day. The enforced limits are more complex. Learn what this means and how to work within them.
- [Introduction to Traceroutes](https://measurementlab.net/kb/introduction-to-traceroutes): How a traceroute reveals the routers between you and a server, how to read its output, why paths are not symmetric, and where to find M-Lab's traceroute data.

### Tests

- [MSAK (Measurement Swiss-Army Knife)](https://measurementlab.net/kb/test-msak): MSAK is M-Lab's configurable multi-stream throughput and UDP latency measurement service — designed for researchers and developers who need more control than single-stream NDT provides.
- [Neubot DASH Streaming Test](https://measurementlab.net/kb/test-neubot-dash): DASH emulates a video streaming player to measure how well a network connection supports adaptive video streaming, without relying on a real video platform.
- [WeHe — Traffic Differentiation Detection](https://measurementlab.net/kb/test-wehe): WeHe tests whether your ISP is treating traffic from specific apps (like YouTube or Spotify) differently from other traffic — detecting throttling or blocking on a per-application basis.
- [Reverse Traceroute](https://measurementlab.net/kb/test-reverse-traceroute): Reverse Traceroute reconstructs the network path from a client back to an M-Lab server — the direction that standard traceroute cannot see — using a distributed system of vantage points and spoofed…
- [Integrating M-Lab Tests into Your Application](https://measurementlab.net/kb/integrating-mlab-tests): How to embed M-Lab's open source tests in a website, mobile app, or software product — and how integration partners can contribute infrastructure back to the M-Lab community.
- [Client-Integration Registration Service (CIRS)](https://measurementlab.net/kb/client-integration-registration-service): What CIRS is, why M-Lab is introducing it, and how usage tiers, costs, and the pilot program work for integrators running tests above the standard rate limits.

### Core Services

- [TCP INFO — M-Lab Core Service](https://measurementlab.net/kb/core-service-tcp-info): TCP INFO collects detailed TCP socket statistics from the Linux kernel for every connection on the M-Lab platform, capturing congestion control state, RTT, loss, and dozens of other metrics at…
- [Packet Headers (PCAP) — M-Lab Core Service](https://measurementlab.net/kb/core-service-packet-headers): M-Lab's packet-headers service captures TCP packet headers for every connection on the M-Lab platform, stored as per-flow .pcap files indexed by UUID.
- [Traceroute — M-Lab Core Service](https://measurementlab.net/kb/core-service-traceroute): M-Lab's Traceroute core service automatically runs a network path measurement from every M-Lab server back to the client for every TCP connection, building a continuous record of Internet routing.

### Accessing Data

- [Getting Started with M-Lab Data in BigQuery](https://measurementlab.net/kb/getting-started-bigquery): How to get free access to M-Lab's BigQuery datasets, run your first queries, understand the data structure, and work efficiently with large tables.
- [FAQ: Accessing M-Lab Data Buckets](https://measurementlab.net/kb/accessing-data-buckets): How to access M-Lab's raw NDT7 data in Google Cloud Storage using gcloud without permission errors.
- [M-Lab Network Annotations: Geolocation, ASNs, and What They Mean](https://measurementlab.net/kb/mlab-annotations-explained): How M-Lab annotates measurements with geographic and network metadata, the accuracy and limitations of each annotation type, and how to use them correctly in analysis.
- [M-Lab Monthly Stats: Pre-computed Parquet Summaries](https://measurementlab.net/kb/monthly-stats-dataset): What the Monthly Stats dataset is, how it's derived from NDT measurements, what the parquet files contain, and how to access them without BigQuery.
- [Reading Percentiles in Monthly Stats](https://measurementlab.net/kb/monthly-stats-percentiles): How to interpret percentile columns in M-Lab Monthly Stats data, including the counterintuitive polarity of latency and loss, and what p50 vs p95 tells you.
- [Exploring Monthly Stats with Python](https://measurementlab.net/kb/monthly-stats-python): A practical guide to loading, filtering, and visualising M-Lab Monthly Stats parquet files in Python using pandas, without needing BigQuery or a Google Cloud account.

### Running a Node

- [Running Your Own M-Lab Node: The BYOS Program](https://measurementlab.net/kb/byos-overview): An overview of M-Lab's Bring Your Own Server program — what it is, what's required, and how hosting a node contributes to global internet measurement.
- [FAQ: IP Address Mismatch in BYOS Environment File](https://measurementlab.net/kb/ip-address-mismatch): How to fix an M-Lab BYOS node that is unreachable due to a mismatch between the env file IP and the server's actual public IP.
- [FAQ: Docker Compose Troubleshooting - Register Node Issues](https://measurementlab.net/kb/register-node-troubleshooting): Steps to diagnose and fix a stopped or unresponsive register-node component in a Docker BYOS deployment.
- [FAQ: Docker BYOS Monitoring and Logging](https://measurementlab.net/kb/docker-byos-monitoring-logging): Recommended Prometheus metrics endpoints and Docker logging configuration to prevent disk exhaustion on M-Lab BYOS nodes.

What we do #

Founded in 2009, Measurement Lab (M-Lab) is an open platform for studying Internet performance and neutrality over time. We provide public, transparent data to empower researchers, policymakers, and open Internet advocates to make informed decisions about Internet infrastructure and policies. M-Lab is a fiscally sponsored project of Superbloom Design.

Global Testing Platform

A network of 425+ servers in 75+ metro areas, hosted at interconnection points and cloud networks.
